### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, touching **7** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via MarketplaceInstallLocalPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **7** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 082f9c2945260fd9b29951caff1c49f6dccab4ea` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c9aab2fc696f33febd74e011c2d2ffe9142b9f80` — the merge of head `1edc890930f3a50cb7331138404cbba4f8858426` into base `082f9c2945260fd9b29951caff1c49f6dccab4ea`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c9aab2fc696f33febd74e011c2d2ffe9142b9f80 && git checkout c9aab2fc696f33febd74e011c2d2ffe9142b9f80
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 082f9c2945260fd9b29951caff1c49f6dccab4ea 1edc890930f3a50cb7331138404cbba4f8858426 && git checkout -B drift-repro 082f9c2945260fd9b29951caff1c49f6dccab4ea && git merge --no-ff 1edc890930f3a50cb7331138404cbba4f8858426

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 082f9c2945260fd9b29951caff1c49f6dccab4ea
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 082f9c2945260fd9b29951caff1c49f6dccab4ea` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

**L1 first review · ACCEPT** · head `1edc890930f3a50cb7331138404cbba4f8858426` (final head 6938564692) · card #34431 · read 2026-11-17T04:43Z

### The one moved answer, and why `Clause-②: no` holds here

On `main` a composed bundle whose package body declares a datasource name another holder owns answers `200` (measured by the dev on `8dd8192cb`, body › Acceptance notes); at this head it answers `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` with nothing written. An input `main` admits is now refused, so I checked whether that refusal is new contract or declared contract. It is declared: `content/docs/data-modeling/external-datasources.mdx` (install-local callout) already publishes "A package declaring a datasource name the runtime already holds is refused `409`", with no carve-out for a composed bundle, and a flat bundle gets exactly that today (the flat control pins it). The `200` was step 2a not reading the package bodies, and the install it answered never registered or connected that datasource. That is a declared-but-unenforced gap closed in the implementation, so the area's call 6938094978 (`Clause-②: no`, option A) stands. This differs from #34531, where the refusal `main` did not give was declared nowhere.

### Checklist (read on GitHub at this head, not from the report)

- **Shape:** draft, base `main`, `Fixes #34431` on line 1; no other closing keyword in the body (`#34432`, `#34403`, `#34407`, `#28143` carry none). Note: the body has no project-attribution lines above the card line; not an L1 item, the seat may add them on its final pass.
- **Declarations:** `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none` in the body and the changeset. No authorable key, schema or export moves. `@objectstack/cloud-connection` is published (`private` unset); the changeset grades it `patch`. No `Skills-docs:` line is owed (no kind, no narrowing arm).
- **File surface:** 3 files from `get_files`: the plugin, the existing #34407 harness test file, the changeset. The pins went into the existing harness as top-level `describe`s instead of a new card-named file, following AGENTS.md's shared-harness placement; accepted.
- **Mechanism, read in the source:**
  - `declaredDatasources(artifact)` keeps the top-level map form, and otherwise reads `resolveStackCollection(artifact, 'datasources')`: the top-level list when present (read once, the flattened-union control pins no per-package repeat), else each body's in package order. It is the one reader for 2a (`findHeldDatasourceName`), the 4b′ connect and the rehydrate.
  - 2a now catches a resolver throw and answers it through `declaredRefusalAnswer` (the 2b / 2c″ reader); an undeclared throw is rethrown.
  - `connectDeclaredDatasources` reads datasources and `objects` through the resolver inside a try that logs at `error` and returns `undefined`, keeping its never-throws contract.
  - `describeInstalledCredentialRefs` reads `resolveStackCollection(converted, 'connectors')`.
  - The removed `Array.isArray(manifest?.i18n)` read: on `origin/main` no producer writes an array `i18n`; every other reader treats it as a config object (`cli/src/commands/serve.ts`, `plugin-dev/src/dev-i18n.ts`, `runtime/src/seed-locale.ts`, `cli/src/utils/stack-collections.ts`). Dead-read removal confirmed.
- **Tests and controls:** 8 new cases on the real route handler and rehydrate. The 2a case asserts `409`, `success: false`, `code: 'RESOURCE_CONFLICT'`, `details: { datasource: 'wms_db' }`, no ledger entry and no connect call; the flat control answers the same. Install, upgrade and rehydrate pins assert the names and objects handed to `connectPackageDatasources` in package order. Red-first on `main` 6 of 16; four ablation legs, each restored to the HEAD blob, each red where predicted.
- **Prose checked against the diff:** the changeset paragraphs ("read those three from the top level only… answered 200", "Step 2a now judges every package body's datasource names… refused `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` before any write", "answered at this step with the resolver's own `422`", the `i18n` sentence) match the code and the pins. No docs page needed a change: the external-datasources callout already states the 409.
- **Gates at this head:** check-runs on `1edc8909…`: 51 runs, 35 `success`, 16 `skipped`, 0 failed; `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check` and `Check Changeset` are `success`. Derived round 71/71 exit 0 at this head (body, `34431-gates-ran.txt`). No dogfood battery owed (no `!`, no narrowing arm).

### Residuals (code-read, no change asked)

- Step 7's `describeInstalledCredentialRefs` resolves `converted` after the write with no guard. For the bytes 2a admitted it should not throw, since 2a resolved the same artifact before any write; a throw there would surface after the install is on disk.
- The dev's out-of-scope note: 2a now resolves `packages` first, so the #34432 pins exercise 2a's refusal and an ablation of 2c″'s incoming-side pre-resolution alone may no longer go red (code-read, not measured). The seat decides whether that is a card under the filing gate.

### Owed after this

- **L2: not owed.** `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, no narrowing arm, no `packages/spec/src/**`, no governed path.
- **Landing tier:** `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 34633` read here: 0 of 3 paths governed, +267 / −15. Not a declared narrowing (reading above). Ordinary queue landing by the area.
